exercise.name: Frog Hip Thrust
aliases: Frog glute bridge on a bench

reference.title: Bodyweight Frog Hip Thrust (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip extension with the hips abducted and externally rotated)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive the hips up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, 0.8 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.progression: Longer squeeze, then a dumbbell or plate on the hips

cues.text: Shoulder blades on the bench edge, arms along the bench. Soles together close to the hips, knees wide.
Breathe out, press the outer edges of the feet down and drive the hips up.
Hips up to about level with the shoulders, pelvis tucked, knees open, chin tucked. Squeeze the glutes.
Breathe in and lower the hips under control, knees staying wide.
Stay on the bench and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop when the trunk is level; ribs down, chin tucked.

mistakes.mistake: Knees closing as the hips rise
mistakes.fix: Keep the thighs open and the soles pressed together.

mistakes.mistake: Feet too far from the hips
mistakes.fix: Heels close to the buttocks; the feet rest on their outer edges.
Pivot on the shoulder blades; the bench edge stays under the same spot.

kinematics.norm: Knee-height bench, about 40-45 cm (common setup; clinical opinion)
Hips reach neutral at the top, trunk level (clinical opinion)
Thighs open and turned out, soles together (defines the frog position; clinical opinion)
Deeply bent with the heels near the hips; more knee bend shifts work from the hamstrings to the glutes in bridges (Lehecka 2017)
About level at the top with the pelvis tucked; the trunk pivots on the shoulder blades (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up, a short squeeze, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #646412, Bodyweight Frog Hip Thrust (male), video (movement reference)

Contreras, Vigotsky, Schoenfeld, Beardsley & Cronin 2015, a comparison of gluteus maximus, biceps femoris and vastus lateralis EMG in the back squat and barbell hip thrust (J Appl Biomech 31(6):452-458)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)
Lehecka et al. 2017, building a better gluteal bridge: EMG of hip muscles during modified single-leg bridges (Int J Sports Phys Ther 12(4):543-549; PMC5534144)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Set the bench against a wall so it cannot slide.
modify: Groin or hip discomfort: narrower knees, feet a little apart.
Low back discomfort: lift less high and brace first.
regressions: Frog glute bridge on the floor.
Two-leg hip thrust with feet flat.
progressions: Dumbbell or plate on the hips.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor and external rotator: the frog position keeps the hips turned out through the whole thrust. The barbell hip thrust gave about twice the mean gluteus maximus activity of the back squat (Contreras 2015); no EMG study of the frog version was found, so the turned-out bias is clinical opinion.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor and external rotator: the frog position keeps the hips turned out through the whole thrust. The barbell hip thrust gave about twice the mean gluteus maximus activity of the back squat (Contreras 2015); no EMG study of the frog version was found, so the turned-out bias is clinical opinion.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Helps hold the thighs open (abduction and external rotation; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Helps hold the thighs open (abduction and external rotation; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension; the soles-together position with deeply bent knees shortens them, so they help less than in a feet-flat thrust (clinical opinion based on Lehecka 2017, where more knee bend lowered hamstring activity in bridges).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension; the soles-together position with deeply bent knees shortens them, so they help less than in a feet-flat thrust (clinical opinion based on Lehecka 2017, where more knee bend lowered hamstring activity in bridges).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Lengthened on the open thighs; they steady the knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Lengthened on the open thighs; they steady the knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Ribs down so the hips, not the low back, lift the pelvis.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Little knee work in this position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Little knee work in this position (clinical opinion).
